summary: beaver-ui-drawer postinstall fetches and executes attacker-controlled binary
details: Package declares postinstall `node setup.js`, which selects a per-OS asset path (`/pkg/package`, `/pkg/loader_mac`, `/pkg/package.exe`) and rotates over five Cloudflare Workers hosts assembled from split strings (`oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev` and siblings 100-416, 101-adf, 102-baf, 103-070) with a DNS fallback under `well1.site` (`tin.dl.well1.site`, `tina.dl.well1.site`, `ldr.dl.well1.site`, `win.dl.well1.site`). setup.js gathers `os.hostname()`, `os.userInfo().username`, `process.cwd()`, Node version and pid as an installId and passes it with the mirror list to `lib/telemetry.js`, which imports child_process via string concatenation (`require('child_' + 'process')`), base64-decodes payload bytes via `Buffer.from(chunks, 'base64')`, stages the file under `/var/tmp` or `%TEMP%`, and marks it executable with `fs['chmod' + 'Sync'](extensionPath, currentMode | parseInt('755', 8))` before spawning it. API and hostname identifiers are split-and-joined at runtime to defeat static analysis. The declared purpose is a UI/visual-components library, unrelated to any binary distribution. Every `npm install` of this version runs an attacker-controlled executable on the installer's machine and beacons a per-host fingerprint to the attacker's infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
